messages.text: Notable Speech clinches City Of York crown for Appleby

metadata.summary: Notable Speech bounced back to his brilliant best to claim his sixth Group One victory in the Sky Bet City of York Stakes.
metadata.content: York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby Charlie Appleby's Notable Speech returned to top form when rocketing to victory in the City Of York Stakes under William Buick, setting up a potential return to America for the Breeders' Cup Mile. Saturday 22 August 2026 15:53, UK Image: William Buick aboard Notable Speech Notable Speech bounced back to his brilliant best to claim his sixth Group One victory in the Sky Bet City of York Stakes. Charlie Appleby's chestnut has been a top-class performer for the last three seasons, with his big-race haul including the 2000 Guineas and Sussex Stakes in 2024, the Woodbine Mile and Breeders' Cup Mile in 2025 and the Lockinge at Newbury this spring. He suffered a rare blip when only sixth as favourite the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot in June, but dropped back to seven furlongs on the Knavesmire - albeit on easier ground than ideal - and showed his true colours in the hands of regular partner William Buick, travelling powerfully before quickening two and three-quarter lengths clear of the chasing pack as the 9-4 favourite. More to follow... messages.text: ​​​​​Russell wins Dutch Sprint to trim title gap to Antonelli

metadata.summary: George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.
metadata.content: Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort George Russell cuts his title deficit to Kimi Antonelli to 56 points with Zandvoort Sprint win; Charles Leclerc passes Lando Norris for second; Lewis Hamilton seventh; watch Qualifying later on at 3pm with Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 14:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race. George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli. The polesitting Russell held the lead from Lando Norris at the start and and withstood an initial challenge from his fellow Briton before the McLaren fell into the clutches of Charles Leclerc's Ferrari behind. Despite being on the more brittle soft tyres compared to the mediums of those around him, Leclerc overtook Norris for second with an impressive move into the first corner on lap 18 of the short-form contest. messages.text: Antonelli to take Monza grid penalty for engine change

metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms Kimi Antonelli to incur grid penalty for exceeding engine parts at Italian GP; championship leader to face at least 10-place penalty at home race in Monza; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 14:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffered a race-ending engine failure in Barcelona World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed. Each driver is permitted a capped amount of various power unit parts for the season, and two separate technical issues for Antonelli have left Mercedes resigned to the fact the Italian will need to exceed the limit before the end of the campaign. If possible, teams will generally choose to incur grid penalties at tracks where overtaking is easier, which is why Mercedes are set to install a new power unit for Antonelli at his home race in Monza from September 4-6.
